decisionBox.changed: Position moves from morning's REDUCE to ADD, and the reason is that morning's own add condition fired on its published mechanics. Morning wrote that a settled 1H close back above 62,846.3 would be the signal to put the tranche back. The 15:00Z bar settled 62,984.7. The desk is honouring its own rule in the direction that is uncomfortable, which is the whole point of writing rules down. Four things need saying plainly. FIRST, morning's LEVELS were right again and its TRADE was wrong again - the same split the desk has logged for two weeks. The 62,685.7 reduce line fired precisely, price fell another 163.9 points below it, and the trim was correct for about two hours before the reversal took it 170.1 points offside. That is now eleven sessions of accurate levels and mostly unprofitable trades. SECOND, this add is deliberately SMALLER than a full reversal of the morning trim, because the OI filter attached to the add gate could not be verified across the 12:00Z-to-17:49Z window: the earlier readings were cached garbage, so there is no honest baseline to difference against. Size down when you cannot check your own condition. THIRD, the futures book stays FLAT and the swing operation stays WAIT. Price sits mid-range between the 62,846.3 reclaim floor and the 63,244.6 session high, 22.1 points below the 1H EMA20 and 305 points below the 1H EMA50 at 63,350.36. Opening leverage in the middle of a 400-point box is the forced bad trade this desk keeps warning itself about, and the 13 August midday short - stopped 306.6 points later at exactly this kind of location - is the cautionary tale on file. FOURTH, what would make this wrong. Brent jumped to 88.480, +1.62% on the day, and the US 10-year backed up 5.4bp to 4.701%; both moved AGAINST risk while BTC was rallying. If the reclaim was a short-covering artefact rather than real demand, that macro pair is what unwinds it, and the tell will be a settled 1H close back under 62,846.3.
